subject: design-technology
title: Biomimicry and Embodied Carbon
welcome_lead: Nature has done the R&D for 3.8 billion years.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: biomimicry, Janine Benyus, and embodied carbon.

concepts.def: Designing systems modelled on biological strategies.
American biologist (b. 1958), coined biomimicry in 1997 book.
Hook-and-loop fastener inspired by burdock burr (1948, de Mestral).
Greenhouse-gas emissions from making a material/product.
UK architects' target for embodied + operational reduction.

walkthroughs.body_html: Janine Benyus's Biomimicry: Innovation Inspired by Nature (1997) codified the field. Nature's strategies — gecko adhesion, lotus self-cleaning, termite cooling — solve problems with chemistry, not energy.

Velcro was invented by Swiss engineer George de Mestral in 1948 after finding burdock burrs stuck to his dog's fur. He observed the hooks under microscope and patented hook-and-loop fastening in 1955.
Embodied carbon (manufacture) and operational carbon (use) together define a building or product's life-cycle GHG. As buildings become operationally efficient, embodied carbon dominates total impact.
